device: Coral USB Accelerator (Google Inc. 18d1:9302), single inference
what: On-device latency for the Re-ID family, in two parts. `backbones` compares the three torchreid architectures the family selects between; `pruning_ladder` is the six reid_youtu_lite rungs that families/re-identification/reid/DELIVERABLE.md offers downstream. Until 2026-08-22 the backbone numbers lived only in outputs/pruning_logs/reid_realdevice_latency.md, which is gitignored, and the ladder had never been measured on a device at all -- DELIVERABLE.md carried a projection.
produced_by: src/etpu/runtime/bench.py, 15 warmup + 100 timed invoke() per model
runtime: tflite_runtime 2.16 + libedgetpu.so.1 delegate inside the edgetpu_ros image, no pycoral. The first invoke() loads Edge TPU firmware (the USB re-enumerates 1a6e:089a -> 18d1:9302); the warmup loop absorbs it.

backbone_findings.operator_count_beats_parameter_count: The device ordering is the inverse of the parameter and accuracy orderings. mobilenetv2_x1_0 holds the most parameters (2.63 MiB on-chip) and is the least accurate (rank-1 85.6%), yet it is the fastest at 2.92 ms -- 70 operators, all dense convolutions. The osnet pair is smaller (0.92-1.86 MiB) and more accurate (92.5-93.7%) and runs 2.7-3.8x slower, at 290 operators each: OSNet's multi-branch LightConv plus channel-gate aggregation lowers into many small operators, each paying its own scheduling cost, and its grouped/depthwise convolutions do not fill the systolic array the way dense convolutions do.
backbone_findings.operator_count_is_not_the_whole_story: 290 operators is the same for both osnet rungs, so it cannot by itself explain 7.97 vs 11.09 ms. The 3.1 ms gap tracks the on-chip parameter bytes (0.92 vs 1.86 MiB) and the MACs behind them. Operator count sets the family's floor; size moves it within the family.
backbone_findings.no_streaming_penalty_at_any_rung: All three compile to off-chip 0.00 B and a single TPU subgraph -- everything fits the 8 MiB parameter cache. The measured 2.9-11.1 ms carries none of the tens-of-milliseconds penalty that streaming weights over USB costs. This is the residency prediction confirmed on the device, on a family where it was never in doubt.
backbone_findings.selection: Lowest latency: mobilenetv2_x1_0 (2.9 ms, rank-1 85.6%). Best accuracy-per-millisecond: osnet_x0_5 (8.0 ms, rank-1 92.5%). Highest accuracy: osnet_x0_75 (11.1 ms, rank-1 93.7%).

backbone_reproducibility: Re-measured 2026-08-22 on the same device against the 2026-07-10 numbers: 2.92 -> 2.923, 8.06 -> 7.969, 11.23 -> 11.094 ms. All three within 1.3% and within a run-to-run std of the original. The 2026-08-22 column is the one this file stands behind.

pruning_ladder_notes.configuration: These six rungs were compiled STANDALONE -- the embedder alone owns the 8 MiB parameter cache. That is not the delivery contract: families/re-identification/reid/DELIVERABLE.md requires co-compiling the embedder with the downstream SSD detector in one edgetpu_compiler call, which leaves the embedder roughly 2.4 MiB. Standalone is therefore the best case, and these numbers are a lower bound on deployed latency.
pruning_ladder_notes.measurement: Compiled from outputs/tflite_int8/reid_youtu_lite_market1501_pruned*_int8.tflite with edgetpu_compiler 16.0.384591198 and benched on the physical Coral on 2026-08-22. Every rung is a single TPU subgraph at 79 operations -- pruning changes the byte budget in this family, not the mapping.
pruning_ladder_notes.family_latency_law: Fitted on these six points: lat_ms = 2.302*offchip_mib + 0.223*onchip_mib + 2.782, R^2 = 0.9976. Residuals -1.20 to +1.46 ms.
pruning_ladder_notes.what_this_corrects: families/re-identification/reid/DELIVERABLE.md projected the co-compile case as off-chip = int8_mib - 2.4 at 3 ms/MiB streamed over a 5 ms base. The off-chip formula is sound; the two constants were not measured. The fit above puts streaming at 2.30 ms/MiB and the base at 2.78 ms, so the published projections ran 30-45% high (~76 -> ~58 ms at the baseline, ~14 -> ~10 ms at the recommended 80% rung). The table now carries both configurations side by side and labels which is measured.
pruning_ladder_notes.cross_family_transfer: The streamed-byte price transfers across architectures and the cached-byte price does not. This repo's line_seg panel (30 models, results/latency_law/) fits 2.260 ms per off-chip MiB; this family independently fits 2.302 -- 1.9% apart, on a different backbone and a different task. The on-chip coefficients are 0.917 and 0.223 and the intercepts 0.861 and 2.782, both far apart, which is expected: those terms absorb each family's own compute, not a transfer rate. Scoring these six rungs against the line_seg law directly gives 1.05-1.39x over-prediction, and the error grows as off-chip falls -- consistent with the mismatch being in the compute terms.
pruning_ladder_notes.two_rungs_are_fully_resident_standalone: At 80% and 90% standalone off-chip is 0.00 B. Under the co-compile contract neither is: at a 2.4 MiB share the 80% rung still streams about 2.97 MiB and the 90% rung about 0.35 MiB. Which number applies depends entirely on whether the embedder is compiled alone.
pruning_ladder_notes.accuracy_provenance: mAP and rank1 are copied from results/reid/sweep_results.json (Market-1501). They were not re-evaluated for this measurement.
pruning_ladder_notes.params_provenance:
params are torch parameter counts of the checkpoints under deliverables/reid_youtu_lite_pruning_sweep/checkpoints_pytorch/; the baseline is 26,655,296. realized_full_pct is the full-model reduction against that baseline, which is what pruned

pct means in this family (unlike line_seg, where it is a channel ratio on the non-_param rungs).

cpu_column_caveat: cpu_int8_ms_x86 was measured on the AVX-512 development host, which is NOT the deployment target. On that host these small int8 models run faster on the CPU than they do across USB to the TPU; the point of the accelerator here is to leave the host CPU free, not to beat it. Do not read the CPU column as a platform-independent number -- only the TPU column is a device absolute. No measurement from the downstream deployment board is recorded in this repository.
accuracy_provenance: market1501_rank1_pct and market1501_mAP_pct are the published torchreid model-zoo figures for these backbones, quoted in families/re-identification/reid/README.md:51. They were not re-evaluated here.
backbones_measured_on: onnx2tf (retired 2026-08-22). The three backbone rows were NOT re-converted: they are architecture comparisons, not ladder rungs, and nothing in results/ fits a law through them. pruning_ladder IS on the current path.

export_path_migration.what: All six pruning_ladder rungs re-converted through litert-torch + ai-edge-quantizer (per-channel), re-compiled and re-benched on the same Coral. tpu_ms_mean_onnx2tf / operations_onnx2tf / int8_mib_onnx2tf keep the previous path's values on each row.
export_path_migration.bytes_unchanged: on-chip and off-chip byte counts are identical rung for rung, to the precision edgetpu_compiler reports. Only the operator count moved, 79 -> 82: a different lowering of the same network. All 82 map to the TPU, 0 on CPU, 1 subgraph, every rung.
export_path_migration.latency_delta_ms: +0.14 to +0.44, every rung slower, no rung by more than 0.44 ms

law_refit.reading: The off-chip coefficient -- the transport rate -- moves 0.36%, and its agreement with the line-seg fit's 2.260 IMPROVES (1.9% -> 1.51%). The whole cost of the export change lands in the intercept (+0.104 ms, the 3 extra operators) and the on-chip term. That is the finding-1 claim surviving a change of converter, not just a change of family.

export_path_migration.gate: This ladder was re-run first, before the other families, precisely to test whether the migration would move the published law. It did not.
export_path_migration.accuracy: NOT re-measured. Re-ID accuracy in this repo is FP32 (results/reid/sweep_results.json is a distillation sweep; the backbone rank1/mAP are quoted torchreid model-zoo figures) -- no int8 accuracy number exists for this family on either path, so the migration owes none.
